A kind and welcoming school
At Woodgrange our culture is built upon a deep understanding of how all young children learn and develop. All children are included and valued.
We provide a high quality, child centred education where all children can thrive.
We believe in nurturing children to become confident, independent, motivated and resilient learners who are curious about the world they live in, and who are imaginative and creative in how they seek answers and tackle challenges.

Who we are
We are a nurturing school in the heart of our community.
Choosing a school for your child is one of the most important decisions you can make. Thank you for visiting our website to find out more about us.
We believe we can offer your child something that is unique, where they will be valued as individuals and where they will truly belong.
We believe children should be allowed to be 3,4,5,6 or 7 years old and that means plenty of time to play, to explore, to follow their interests, to solve problems, to be creative, curious, collaborative and resilient. We focus on developing language, motivation, awareness of self and others and independence. These are all essential life skills for a rapidly changing world.
Our staff team are highly skilled at building the warm, trusting relationships that are essential for children to thrive.
Alongside our playful approach is rigorous teaching of core skills and an engaging curriculum designed to help children develop as learners, love reading, have no fear of numbers and know how to find “stuff out” rather than be told.
Come and join us on our journey!
What people say about us

Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural Curriculum Fundamental British Values
We believe that our pupils should be encouraged and enabled to think deeply and reflect on their learning and understanding. We will challenge ideas with our pupils and help them to be able to articulate their views and debate others.
With regard to British Values we believe that the four principles underpin what we do every day. Through our curriculum we aim to give children a rounded understanding of how these principles were reached:
We believe in giving our pupils having many opportunities for their voices to be heard. These include through:
The importance of rules, whether they be those that govern the class, the school, or the country, are consistently reinforced throughout the school day. Pupils are taught the value and reasons behind rules and are involved in devising them, that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken.
Visits from authorities such as the Police and Fire Service help reinforce this message.
Within school, pupils are actively encouraged to make choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. As a school we educate and provide boundaries for young pupils to make choices safely, through provision of a safe environment and empowering education. Pupils are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and advised how to exercise these safely, for example through our online-Safety lessons.
Whether it be through their choice of lunches, learning partners or challenges, or their choice of participation in our numerous extra-curricular clubs and opportunities, pupils are given the freedom to make meaningful choices.
Children learn that their behaviour has an effect on their own rights and those of others. All members of the school community treat each other with respect.
Children are taught to accept each other for who they are and to not discriminate against those who look, act, talk or dress differently.
Children in the Early Years are explicitly taught empathy.
Tolerance of those of Different Faiths and Beliefs
Woodgrange is situated in a culturally diverse area therefore we place a great emphasis on sharing experiences and promoting mutual understanding and respect.
Children are involved in celebrating each others’ special days and visiting places of worship that are important to different faiths.
At Woodgrange we celebrate that which keeps us together rather than that which may separate us.
At Woodgrange we will actively challenge pupils or parents expressing opinions contrary to fundamental British Values.
Our playful approach reinforces these values as we provide freedom with guidance, allowing children to:
Debates about big questions
Choosing learning partners
Directing their own learning

pageCache.text:
We offer an inclusive and enriched curriculum to develop all aspects of learning for children. We have a dedicated and skilled staff body who work hard with our governors and parents to promote good progress and attainment for all. We have high expectations of everyone in our school and value their contribution.
Our aims are for all children:
Adults in school are all committed to supporting children to develop these skills and attributes.
At Woodgrange we endeavour to meet the needs of everyone in our school. We believe in the inherent equality of all individuals, irrespective of physical or mental ability, gender or race, and reflect these both in the learning opportunities we offer the children and in the general manner in which all those who come into contact with our school are treated.
We wholeheartedly endorse the Borough’s Equal Opportunities policy.
Anti-Racist Statement
The school is opposed to any form of racism and racist behaviour. All children have the right to the best possible education. This means recognising the varied cultural backgrounds of the children and reflecting them in a positive way throughout the life of our school and our curriculum.
We are determined that all children will see themselves and their lived experiences reflected and represented positively at school.
The school has ensured that diversity is woven into all books it uses across the curriculum. – OFSTED 2025

pageCache.text:
Play can develop determination, concentration persistence and a satisfying sense of ‘I did it!’
Nursery and Reception
Children have extended opportunities to learn through play. Learning takes place both inside and outside and the classroom. Through a mixture of carefully planned adult activities and more spontaneous child led activities the children develop skills and understanding in the following 7 areas of learning:
The Prime Areas of Learning are
Personal, Social and Emotional Development (PSED)
Children are encouraged to establish positive relationships with adults and other children. They learn to work co-operatively as part of a group, to understand what is right and wrong and why and to consider the consequences of their actions. Adults working in early years aim to encourage all children, to make sure that each child is given an equal chance to join in with the range of activities on offer and that all children feel equally valued as part of the whole group.
Communication and Language (CL)
Children have had the opportunities to develop their speaking and listening, reading and writing skills by sharing and enjoying many stories, rhymes and non-fiction books. We have a strong focus on early language development through play, role play and story telling.
Physical Development (PD)
Children use a range of balancing and climbing apparatus to develop their co-ordination and awareness of space. They use a variety of sports equipment in play, learning to play with others and to navigate space and movement.
We also focus on using smaller tools, construction and malleable materials to practise fine motor skills
The Specific Areas of Learning are:
Children learn about pattern, shape, and measures. They order, sequence and sort with objects and numbers through practical activities.
They are encouraged to use mental strategies and skills as well as number rhymes, songs and games. We follow a mastery approach, ensuring a deep understanding and solid foundation in number sense.
Understanding the World (UW)
This area of learning includes science, history, geography, design technology, and religious education. We focus on providing the children with a range of activities and different equipment to investigate and use.
Children experience cooking, woodwork and modelling or construction toys. Through visits and experiences such as planting seeds or watching eggs hatch children develop their understanding of the natural world. We will soon be building a pond. Through discussion and sharing experiences we help children develop their sense of the different faiths, cultures and traditions their community encompasses as well as their personal history.
Expressive Arts and Design (EAD)
Children explore colour, shape, texture, form and space through a range of activities in art, music, dance, stories and imaginative play. We provide them with opportunities to express and communicate their ideas and feelings. Each term they look at the work of different artists and create their own art using paint, drawing, collage or clay.
Children come to school with different experiences and progress at different rates and some children will need additional support with some aspects of their learning, whilst others need extra challenges. This is provided by a skilled staff team.
Children’s progress is carefully monitored through Nursery and Reception and learning tailored to their needs and interests. Teachers will share children’s next steps with you at parents’ evenings as well as being available before school each day.
At the end of the Reception year children’s progress is assessed against the Early Learning Goals and the Early Years Foundation Stage Profile.
Our Nursery class is situated at the rear of school under the shelter of one of the tallest trees in Newham.
Children can attend for 15 hours a week- 5 3 hour sessions or for 30 hours if parents are eligible.
The caring staff ensure children are settled and happy and develop their readiness for school through playful interactions that develop language and early skills that are the foundations for learning in Reception.
Most, but not all children go on to “big school” with us. Attendance at our nursery does not guarantee a school place. We are happy to show parents the classroom and dedicated outdoor space upon request.
In our 4 Reception classes children begin their full time education. We spend time getting to know them and making sure they are settled and happy.
Within the first 6 weeks of school teachers carry out the national “Baseline” assessments. They are short assessments of school readiness, carried out 1:1.
Over the year children are taught through a blend of short whole class sessions – phonics (for reading) and maths and adult supported play.
We see children rapidly develop the skills needed for reading, writing and maths as well as developing confidence, independence and curiosity about the world which ensures their readiness for the Key Stage 1 curriculum.
We have a strong focus on wellbeing and language development which are both brilliantly supported by our playful approach.
At the end of the year the children’s development is assessed against the “Early learning goals”.
Transition into Year 1 is supported by visits to the “big playground” and the children meet their new teacher in their new classroom.
